subject: Math
prompt: A laboratory technician added a chemical solution to a beaker at a constant rate. After $2$ seconds, the volume of the chemical solution in the beaker was $50$ milliliters. After $4$ seconds, the volume of the chemical solution in the beaker was $90$ milliliters. The equation $V = 20t + 10$ gives the volume $V$, in milliliters, of the chemical solution in the beaker in terms of the time $t$, in seconds, since the technician began adding the solution. What is the best interpretation of $10$ in this context?

choices.A: The time, in seconds, at which the volume of the chemical solution in the beaker reached $10$ milliliters
choices.B: The rate, in milliliters per second, at which the technician added the chemical solution to the beaker
choices.C: The volume, in milliliters, of the chemical solution that was in the beaker before the technician began adding the solution
choices.D: The total volume, in milliliters, of the chemical solution in the beaker after $10$ seconds

explanation: The equation $V = 20t + 10$ is in the form $V = mt + b$, where $b$ represents the value of $V$ when $t = 0$. When $t = 0$ (before the technician began adding solution), $V = 20(0) + 10 = 10$ milliliters. Therefore, $10$ represents the initial volume of chemical solution that was already in the beaker before the technician began adding more solution.
